Much more current evidence than LastUpdated (2024-07-16) found and it CONFIRMS idle, though the story is more dramatic than the sheet reflects. Timeline reconstructed from the PHMSA CAO and press: the pipeline had been shut-in and nitrogen-filled since 2012 (see the Stop fill/concern re: 2011-vs-2012). Delfin, working toward reactivating it as feedgas infrastructure for its Delfin FLNG deepwater export project (which reached a reported ~$5B FID around June 2026 per press coverage not independently re-verified in this pass), was running a cleaning pig with an in-line inspection tool through the line on Feb 3, 2026 when the pig struck a closed valve, gas was re-injected/ignited, and the line RUPTURED near Mae's Beach/Johnson Bayou -- a fire 50-80 ft wide burned for hours, ~56 MMcf of gas was released, one worker was injured (later suing Delfin, Genesis and others -- Kherkher Garcia LLP suit, Harris County), and Johnson Bayou High School (6 mi away) briefly sheltered in place. PHMSA issued Corrective Action Order CPF 4-2026-028-CAO on Feb 6, 2026 (case status OPEN per primis.phmsa.dot.gov), confirming as of that date: 'The pipeline is currently shut-in and not operating' and capping any eventual restart at 20% of MAOP pending a third-party investigation, remedial work plan, and hydrostatic testing (first progress report due April 1, 2026; case remains open as of this Sept 2026 review with no restart confirmed in any source found). NET: the pipeline never actually returned to service during this incident -- it ruptured WHILE being prepared for reactivation, and remains shut-in. 'idle' is therefore still the correct Status, now with dramatically fresher and more detailed evidence than the sheet had. Recommend also watching for a status change to 'construction' or 'operating' once/if PHMSA authorizes restart -- no evidence of that as of the most recent sources found (Feb 2026).

I searched specifically for post-2023 confirmation (Asheville Citizen Times, Asheville Watchdog, Mountain Xpress, EIA pipeline-projects workbooks, NCUC docket search) and could not find one — NCUC's docket-detail pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetch, which is the main gap; a human search of starw1.ncuc.gov or the Buncombe/Dominion 'T-072' CPCN docket directly would likely close it. Given the weight of the schedule + elapsed-time + absent-from-current-projects-list evidence, I am proposing the change to 'operating' at tier=medium (not high, since no single source states the fact directly) rather than leaving this 'stale' — the dormancy rules are a poor fit for a project that was already ~92% physically built and fully permitted for its last segment, as opposed to a project with no construction activity.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's operators/owners tab records Owner1="Venture Global LNG" at 100%, with no ref. Every independent source found (Kinder Morgan's own February 2020 Evangeline Pass Expansion Project fact sheet PDF, Natural Gas Intelligence, Coeus Energy) describes Venture Global LNG only as the customer/off-taker buying incremental firm transportation capacity for its Plaquemines LNG terminal -- never as an equity owner of the Evangeline Pass pipeline facilities. ("SNG"), a Delaware limited liability company equally owned by subsidiaries of Kinder Morgan, Inc. and Southern Company, are proposing the Evangeline Pass Expansion Project.' It then lists the specific new/modified facilities: the two loop segments that sum to this row's 13.1-mile length are BOTH explicitly along existing TGP lines (Yscloskey Toca Lateral in St. Bernard Parish; the 500 Line in Plaquemines Parish), and Coeus Energy's June 3, 2025 article confirms Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. itself filed for and received FERC's final in-service authorization (May 29, 2025) for the last of these segments (the 4-mile Plaquemines Parish loop). resolutions.researcher_notes: Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC and Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC are two DISTINCT FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas companies, both historically part of Columbia Pipeline Group and both now subsidiaries of TC Energy -- easy to conflate (as GEM's own sheet appears to have done here) but legally and operationally separate entities with separate FERC dockets, separate tariffs, and non-overlapping (if geographically adjacent/interconnected) pipeline systems. Every independent source found for the Louisiana XPress Project names Columbia GULF, never Columbia Gas: (1) FERC's Certificate Order captions the applicant as 'Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC,' Docket No. CP19-488-000, and states 'Columbia Gulf is part of Columbia Pipeline Group Inc., which is a subsidiary of TC Energy Corporation' -- Columbia Gas is never mentioned in the order; (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset records `pipeline_operator_name = 'Columbia Gulf Transmission'` for this exact project (docket CP19-488) in all 23 releases from July 2019 through August 2026; (3) Natural Gas Intelligence's 2022 article states explicitly: 'TC Energy affiliate Columbia Gulf said it needs until Dec. 31 to construct and make available for service the Shelburn Compressor Station, the final one to be built for the Louisiana XPress Project (LAXP) [CP19-488]'; (4) 1012industryreport.com's trade-press piece on the project also names Columbia Gulf Transmission; (5) TC Energy's own public fact sheet for the project is titled 'About Columbia Gulf Transmission' and states 'TC Energy's Columbia Gulf Transmission stretches 3,368 miles, starting in Kentucky and continuing through Tennessee, Mississippi, and Louisiana' -- immediately followed by the Louisiana XPress Project map and timeline on the same document. Five independent origins (federal regulator's order, federal EIA dataset, two separate trade-press outlets, and the operator's own public materials), zero of which name Columbia Gas Transmission for this project. CAVEAT: on 2023-10-04, TC Energy completed the sale of a 40% non-controlling equity interest in both Columbia Gas AND Columbia Gulf (as a combined package) to Global Infrastructure Partners (TC Energy's own announcement, tcenergy.com/announcements/2023/2023-10-04-...). Not treated as a spec/duplicate issue -- this is a corporate-attribution correction, not a physical-existence or double-count problem.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Capacity disagreement between the sheet/EIA and the primary FERC filing.
